explanation: As the land slowly rose, the river kept cutting down through layer upon layer of rock, so the deeper the layer, the older the rock.

claims.text: The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon.
The Rio Grande, the Columbia River and the Mississippi River do not flow through the Grand Canyon.
The Colorado River cut the Grand Canyon as the surrounding land was slowly uplifted.
In the Grand Canyon, deeper rock layers are older than the layers above them.

evidence.restatement: The Grand Canyon in Arizona was cut by the Colorado River.
The Rio Grande, the Columbia and the Mississippi flow far from the Grand Canyon; only the Colorado runs through it.
The Colorado River cut down into the canyon as the Colorado Plateau was slowly uplifted.
The canyon's rocks follow superposition: the deepest layers exposed are the oldest.
The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon in Arizona.
The Rio Grande (Texas-Mexico border), the Columbia (Pacific Northwest) and the Mississippi (central US) do not flow through the Grand Canyon.
The Colorado Plateau was slowly uplifted while the Colorado River cut down through the rock, forming the canyon.
Sedimentary strata are deposited in sequence, so deeper layers in the canyon walls are older.
